q: Design a claims fraud detection system.
a: Score claims at FNOL via an API and re-score nightly as documents arrive; features from a feature store (history, network, timing, amounts, text); XGBoost with class weights, time-split validation and calibration; capacity-based threshold to an SIU queue with SHAP reasons; outcomes as labels with random audits; monitor drift, hit rate and fairness.

q: How do you choose the fraud threshold?
a: From investigator capacity and costs, not F1: if SIU reviews 150 claims/week out of 14,000, flag the top ~1.1% and measure precision/recall in that top k.

q: Why is accuracy useless for fraud?
a: With 1–2% fraud, predicting 'no fraud' for everything is 98–99% accurate. Use PR-AUC and precision/recall at the operating point.

q: What label problems exist in fraud data?
a: Labels arrive late, only investigated claims are labelled (selection bias), and 'not proven' isn't 'genuine'. Use random audits and careful handling of unlabelled claims.
